subject: crab
pitch: A feisty red rock crab with one oversized claw raised in challenge. A wide, knobbly shell in brick red speckled with orange and cream, eyes on stalks, eight jointed walking legs with pointed tips, and claws with dark tips and little teeth on the pinchers. A tiny barnacle and a strand of seaweed cling to the back of its shell.
reasoning:
I'm planning out a rock crab model in TypeScript, sketching its scale, orientation, and skeleton structure with a root body joint before building out the limbs and claws.

The carapace will be a flattened ellipsoid sphere with mottled red-orange-cream paint patterns and scattered knob bumps across its surface. For the eyes, I'm using small rods with spheres on top as stalks mounted near the front of the shell, aimed outward and upward. The legs need four per side built as multi-segment limbs (coxa, merus, carpus, propodus, dactyl style), working out the hip-to-foot distances and segment lengths so the knee bends point upward and outward correctly.

Still working out the leg chains...

Working out the big claw geometry — placing the arm joints up through elbow and wrist, then building the palm as a scaled ellipsoid with a fixed and movable pincer finger, defining positions and directions in model space.

Still working out the claw geometry...

I realize it's simpler to avoid posing the jaw entirely and instead build the movable finger's geometry directly in its open position, with the joint aimed along the tilted opening direction from the start—no rotation math needed afterward.

For the claw helper itself, I'll attach a hand joint at the parent arm's tip (wrist), keeping the chain naming simple, then build the claw geometry in the hand's local frame scaled appropriately.

Placing the palm sphere scaled and oriented along the hand's local axis, using the hand frame directly so position and rotation inherit correctly...

Now working out the fixed finger as a bezier sweep from a base point near the hand to its tip, with tapering radii and a darker band near the tip, then setting up the movable pincer joint anchored at another local hand point...

Still writing pincer finger geometry...

Still computing finger geometry...

Still placing arm joints...

I should double-check floor clearance and claw height against the leg span, then add jaw/mouthpart bones under the body and eye stalk joints as children, keeping proportions consistent with the overall body scale.

Now I'm sketching the eye stalks as rods ending in small spheres with dark pupils, and shaping the carapace as a wide ellipsoid with lateral spines and a rimmed edge for the crab's shell silhouette.

Placing side spines around the shell edge using azimuth angles, then scattering knobs across the top in alternating orange and cream colors for texture variety before moving on to the barnacle details.

Adding small cream cone frustums clustered on the rear of the shell for barnacles, then sprouting a few seaweed strands from nearby hit points using curved sweeps with tapering widths and green coloring, including subtle droop and tiny bladder details for realism.

Now I'm setting the resting pose with spread legs, letting the bone chains auto-generate sweeps along each limb. For leg coloring I'm mottling a brick/orange paint with a darker band near the tips, then laying out hip and foot positions per leg so the front pair reaches forward while the back pair trails behind.

For limb geometry I'm computing segment lengths that sum beyond the hip-to-foot distance so the legs bend naturally, then specifying explicit bend directions for each inner joint of the three-segment limb rather than relying on a single shared direction value.

I'm checking that the hip joint sits properly inside the shell's ellipsoid boundary by computing the shell's radius at the hip's x-position, confirming the hip at y=0.04 is within range so the leg emerges naturally from under the shell near x≈0.11.

Naming each leg's joints (hip/knee/ankle/foot per leg index) and tapering the leg segment radii so they narrow toward a point tip, while placing small spheres at the knee joints attached to the correct bone reference.

Now adding a flatter, darker cream belly ellipsoid under the shell, setting the root body joint and shell center positions, and defining the color palette (brick, orange, cream, dark, deep red) to apply layered spot patterns onto the shell surface.

I'm working out the paint composition logic, confirming that nested paints like spots within spots work correctly since every color argument accepts a paint function, and planning to use countershade to give the belly and legs/claws a lighter variant of the shell coloring. Now starting to write the claw-building function that chains arm segments from shoulder to elbow to wrist using catmull-rom splines.

Still writing claw function...

Settling on a brick-red color string for the rod bands. For the teeth, I'm computing their positions by interpolating along the finger rod in local coordinates, blending y and z values with a radius factor so each tooth sits properly offset from the core line before placing it as a part.

Now I'm setting up the movable pincer joint, defining its pivot location and direction relative to the hand bone, then building the pincer rod and its own set of teeth using the same local-coordinate interpolation approach.

I'm adding a small hinge-like base sphere at the pincer joint and assigning it a "hinge" role, then defining the crab's jaw as a separate joint on the body with its own lower and upper parts. After double-checking element counts, I'm scattering knobs across the shell's upward-facing surface using a filtered random distribution, alternating small embedded spheres in different colors for texture.

Next I'm placing edge spikes by sampling surface points around the shell, then growing seaweed strands from a rear surface point—building multiple drooping catmull-rom curves that drape backward and downward, swept into thin green tapered shapes with pointed ends to look organic.
